outcome.technical: R5 (tools/sweep-selftests.py): block_figure now gives a block with no figure in a suite that has block figures the larger of the even share (`suite`) and the suite's largest recorded block, ghost labels included (new basis `largest`). block_timeout, unit_costs, work_items and shard_units all read it. budget_line counts `largest` blocks by name, and shard_line counts every basis. Docstrings and the shards/blocks model comments were updated. bk1's z-block expectation moved from (900, suite) to (1200, largest), because the old expectation encoded the bug. New bk5: a fixture rename gives (1800, 'largest'), and on the live table, renaming test_drive_phase.py's heaviest block (ar-block) keeps its timeout (1789, now 'largest'). bk5 also checks that the budget line counts it. bk2's y (share 500 > largest 400 -> 1500, suite) is the second direction. R6 (tests/_harness.py), design: the check reads the source rather than the runs. New _written_id / block_written_ids / cross_block_ids read, off the AST, every check() call whose first argument spells a literal id. They follow each STAGES row through every top-level function it names, called or passed on. An id written on two lines that two different blocks reach is a failing case naming each line and block. stage_faults returns these, so every full staged run and every --replay reads them, whichever blocks a part was dealt. New sr3c (static reading: k1 and k5 caught through a helper of one block; a shared line, two lines of one block and a runtime-built id are not flagged). New sr21 (a real fixture suite: a part that ran only d-block, with e-block elsewhere, still fails DUPLICATE CASE ID `z1` ACROSS BLOCKS). Why this over the alternative (each part prints its call-site map and a later job joins the parts): the fault is a property of the authored source, and the source is identical in every part. The join would need a new CI job plus artifacts and a verify.sh slice (verify.sh is not in this task's files), and it would only see sites from parts that finished. Measured on all live staged suites: cross_block_ids finds nothing on HEAD. Limit, stated in the code: an id built at runtime is read only where both blocks share a run. The runtime call-site check stays. ci.yml: only a comment naming where the check lives. No new step or job, so no new `longest` line; the 4-shard matrix line and timeout-minutes are untouched. gate-parity.py was not edited. Dependants: ci.yml selftests matrix and bounds unchanged, and gate-parity is green. prove-gates' shard_matrix_drift anchor line is unchanged, and prove-gates --selftest is 61/61. stamp-verification.py reads only the file-level `costs` and TIMEOUT_PER_COST, both unchanged, so it is still correct. tt5 is green: a missing block's bound is at most its suite's largest block, which is at most the untimed bound. sd2 is green: block_figure changes weights, not membership. test_drive_phase's _harness._load_sweep is unchanged. The full local sweep is 193/193 files ok with exit 0. Its budget line shows 316 blocks from their own figure and 0 on any fallback. Left for another task (not my files): CLAUDE.md:238 and :251 and CONTRIBUTING.md:331 and :347 still describe a missing block's fallback as only its suite's figure over its blocks. They now owe 'or its suite's largest recorded block when that is more'.
outcome.descriptive: A renamed or added block is never timed tighter than its suite's heaviest recorded block. Duplicate case ids across a staged suite's blocks are read off the source by every replay, so every CI part checks them.
